title: Abstract classes versus interfaces
answer: An abstract class is a partially implemented class: it can hold instance state, define constructors, expose concrete or abstract instance methods, and participate in single class inheritance. An interface primarily defines a capability contract and supports multiple implementation inheritance; it can also provide default, static, and private methods, but it does not provide ordinary per-object instance fields or constructors.
